item.title: DQC Theory Seminars: Accessing and preparing spacelike vacuum entanglement in scalar quantum fields — Wed Sep 30, 2:00 PM — Gross Hall 324
item.description:
Abstract: Negativity is an important bipartite entanglement measure, which we show to be necessary and sufficient for a broad class of physical mixed states, including disjoint regions of the many-body vacuum. Guided by the structure of the negativity contributing subspace, we define an entanglement class to which the reduced state of the disjoint regions belongs, enabling the calculation of optimal interaction profiles for extracting entanglement between disjoint regions. When measurements and classical communication with the remaining volume are allowed, entanglement between disjoint vacuum regions can be purified. We establish a protocol for quantitatively determining the projective measurements and the resulting purified entanglement between disjoint regions, finding that the minimum and maximum achievable pure entanglement decay exponentially faster and slower than the classical correlations present in the vacuum.
The DQC Theory Seminars meet every other Wednesday from 2:00-3:00

item.title: OpenAI: Beyond the Basics: What’s New in ChatGPT — Wed Sep 30, 6:00 PM — None
item.description:
You may already use ChatGPT to brainstorm, summarize or get a head start on a project. But there's a lot more you can do with the version available to you at Duke.
Join OpenAI for an hour-long virtual session designed for students to explore the latest models, powerful new features, and what's possible with ChatGPT beyond just chatting.

item.description:
The Laboratory for Social Choreography invites you to participate in its latest venture, Theater.
Spend an evening in meaningful conversation with strangers. Listen, speak, disagree, remain silent, and encounter others without judgment or fear. Discover what the collective body is thinking and dreaming about.

item.title: DICE Book Launch and Discussion: Sick Work — Thu Oct 1, 10:00 AM — Rubenstein Library Holsti-Anderson Family Assembly Room 153
item.description:
Please join the Disability Inclusion and Community Empowerment (DICE) Affinity Group, Duke University Press, and the Department of Cultural Anthropology for the book launch of "Sick Work: Exhaustion, Labor, and Invisible Illness" by Dr. Emily Lim Rogers, Assistant Professor of Cultural Anthropology. This event is being held in recognition of National Disability Employment Awareness Month, and Dr. Rogers will be in conversation with Dr. Catherine Clune-Taylor, Assistant Professor of Gender, Sexuality, and Feminist Studies.
From the book jacket:
In "Sick Work," Emily Lim Rogers shows the unpaid labor it takes to be recognized as sick in the United States. Through a historical and ethnographic account of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS)-a disease defined by disproportionate exhaustion after any form of exertion, which has no cure or treatment-she reveals how changing formations of labor decide what counts as disability and what does not. item.description:

Make sure that your bike is in good working order - tires hold air and are up to pressure, brakes and shifters work and your chain has been oiled. The end of the season is fast approaching. We'll be riding just over 1 hour and about 12 miles. The ride is fairly flat and shaded and our pace will be moderate (about 12 mph average). I recommend a hard tail or hybrid bike, but if you really want to bring a road bike it's ok, though you'll likely be a bit bored. Unicycles....?
I'll be eating after the ride at a restaurant. You're welcome to join me if you like.

Be sure to bring your flashlight as the hike will conclude after sunset.
At least 0.5 miles of hiking is off trail with one creek crossing and a fair amount of elevation change. This hike is moderate to difficult. All children must be accompanied by an adult.
